title: Lazur vs Superwhisper on Mac in 2026: offline or an assistant that sees your screen
metaTitle: Lazur vs Superwhisper on Mac: which one fits your work in 2026
description: Lazur vs Superwhisper for Mac: offline, tunable dictation or a voice assistant that sees your screen. Prices and platforms from each company's own site.
intro: Superwhisper is a dictation app for Mac, Windows, iPhone and Android, and it can transcribe offline with on-device models. Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that also dictates. It sees your screen, answers out loud and points at things. Choose by what you need: offline, tunable dictation, or help with the app in front of you.
tldr: Superwhisper is a dictation app. Lazur is a voice assistant that also dictates.
Pick Superwhisper for offline, on-device transcription and more devices.
Pick Lazur for answers about your screen, pointing at buttons and step-by-step help.
Superwhisper Pro starts at $8.49 per month. Lazur Pro is $18 per month after a 3-day trial.

blocks.text: Superwhisper alternative or Lazur: what each app does on Mac

Superwhisper is built to put your words on the page. You hold a key, speak, and clean text lands in the app in front of you. Lazur dictates too, but it also looks at your screen when you ask. It answers out loud, points at things and walks you through the next click.

The difference shows up when you get stuck. Dictation helps when you already know what to write. An assistant helps when you cannot find a setting or do not understand a message on screen. If you only need the words, dictation is enough.

Both apps type into any Mac app. The real split is what happens after you speak. Superwhisper turns speech into text, then applies the mode you picked. Lazur answers questions, points at things and handles small jobs like timers and reminders.
Dictation quality: which app types what you say

Superwhisper's strength is control over the dictation engine. Its Free plan includes unlimited dictation with local Whisper models, custom vocabulary and text replacements. Pro adds cloud voice models, realtime transcription and bring-your-own API keys.

Reviewers say much the same. A tl;dv review published June 21, 2026 praised solo dictation and the custom vocabulary panel. The same review criticized proper nouns and a default cleanup step that sometimes changed meaning. Tl;dv sells a meeting tool, so read that review with that in mind.

Lazur keeps dictation simple. Hold fn and speak. Lazur writes clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. You also get snippets, a personal dictionary and clipboard slots. Dictation is included in both plans and is unlimited on each.

Dictation is not the headline for Lazur. If your work is mostly transcription with tuned models, Superwhisper gives you more settings to turn. Lazur gives you fewer settings and more help around the words.
Offline dictation on Mac: where Superwhisper leads

Superwhisper is the offline choice of this pair. Its homepage says it works offline, so you can transcribe anytime. Its privacy policy, updated October 8, 2026, says that when you use a local model, your audio and transcripts never leave your device.

Lazur is not an offline app. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about the screen, and Lazur sends the audio and the screenshot to AI providers to answer. Nothing is stored. Lazur says content is never used to train AI models. It listens and looks only while you hold the shortcut.

Offline matters in a few real places. A train with no signal. A client office where audio cannot leave the room. A hotel Wi-Fi you do not trust. If one of those describes your week, Superwhisper fits better.

Check your Mac before you buy. The homepage says offline models really run well only on Apple silicon Macs. It also says Intel Macs work best with cloud models. Open Menu bar icon > Settings to see which model is selected.

Cloud models are a different promise. Superwhisper says cloud audio is processed in memory and is not stored after the request completes. Third-party models process it under their own terms. Read those terms before you send client material through a cloud model.
A common mistake is assuming every mode stays on the device. A mode with AI processing or a cloud model sends your words out. Pick the model on purpose, then dictate.
Lazur vs Superwhisper pricing: what each plan costs

Superwhisper's Free plan is usable, not a teaser. It includes unlimited dictation with local models and up to 2 modes with no AI processing. Pro adds file transcription, unlimited modes, cloud models, Meetings on macOS and bring-your-own API keys.

Superwhisper lists Monthly $8.49 per month, Annual $84.99 per year (saves about 17%) and Lifetime $249.99 one-time. Every plan includes the same features, and only the billing differs. That price comes from its official plans page.

Lazur's Pro plan costs $18/month, or $15/month billed annually, and includes 150 AI actions. Power costs $120/month, or $96/month billed annually, and includes 1,000 AI actions. Dictation is unlimited on both. Lazur does not list a lifetime plan.

Monthly prices are only part of the picture. A lifetime license can beat a monthly plan after enough months. Work out the break-even yourself, using the prices above and the months you expect to keep the app.

Trials differ. Superwhisper gives new users 3,000 words of free access to all Pro features, including Meetings. When the words run out, the app falls back to Free and nothing is deleted. Lazur gives a 3-day Pro trial with no credit card. The trial starts when you first open the app.

Superwhisper has a clear refund window. Individual plans have a 30-day refund window from the date of first purchase. Renewal charges are not refundable on their own. The plans page does not state a refund policy, so read the manage subscription page too.

Cancelling is simple on Superwhisper. Pro features stay on until the end of your billing period, then the account moves to Free. Custom modes, vocabulary and history stay on the device. App Store subscriptions must be managed through Apple.
Superwhisper platforms: Windows, iPhone and Android

Superwhisper runs on Mac, Windows 10 and 11, iPhone with iOS 26 or later, and Android phones. Android tablets are not supported. One Pro license covers unlimited Macs and Windows PCs, plus iPhone and Android phones.
Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available. If you need the same assistant on a Windows laptop or an iPhone, Lazur is not the choice today.

The Windows app is not a copy of the Mac app. Superwhisper's docs list Mac features missing on Windows, including coding-agent integrations and the CLI. Windows uses a Meeting mode with system audio instead of the full Meetings feature.

Android is a newer story. Modes and vocabulary are stored per device and do not sync yet. Superwhisper says cloud sync is planned. A mode you set up on your Mac will need setting up again on your phone.
The homepage footer also names Linux. We could not confirm a Linux app, so treat Linux as unverified.
Screen help: where Lazur is the better pick

Lazur sees your screen when you hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask. It answers out loud. Ask where something is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something, and it guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click.

Here is a real case. You need a setting in Apple menu > System Settings > Keyboard, but the layout looks different after an update. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask where the setting is. Lazur circles it. You click, then ask for the next step.

Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you. It is not a plugin or add-in for any app, and it has no partnership with any app maker. Expect guidance, not automation. The next click stays yours.

Superwhisper's Pro plan lists context awareness and AI-powered modes. Its plans do not list pointing at buttons or walking you through an app. If you want help with the app in front of you, Lazur is built for that job.
Everyday tasks and background research on Mac

Lazur handles everyday actions by voice. Set timers, use Apple Reminders, create Calendar events, write notes, control music and volume, open apps and links, search the web and run Shortcuts. Lazur keeps a memory of what you asked and did, on the Mac.
Research runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs through the Lazur for Chrome extension. It comes back with a summary and a report. You give the job and let it run in the background.

Superwhisper's Pro plan leans toward transcription and meetings. It adds file transcription, system audio recording, speaker separation and full Meetings on macOS. Google Calendar meeting support arrived in version 3.2.0 on November 5, 2026.

Meetings are where Superwhisper pushes hardest. Lazur does not list meeting recording, so if you record calls every day, Superwhisper is the better fit. A tl;dv reviewer found no speaker labels in an earlier build. The plans page now lists speaker separation, so test it yourself.
A normal workday with each app

Take a Tuesday. You write three client emails, take a call and need a reminder for Thursday. With Superwhisper, you hold the key and dictate each email, using a mode such as Email. The reminder is still on you to set.
With Lazur, you dictate the emails with hold fn. Then you hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask for the reminder. Lazur adds it to Apple Reminders. If you forget where a Mail setting lives, you ask, and Lazur circles it.
Most days, the honest answer is both. Dictation does the bulk of the typing. The assistant handles the small questions that interrupt it. If you only dictate, you will not need the second app.
Dictation speed and accuracy: what the numbers show

Speed claims are easy to overstate. A 2016 lab study on an iPhone 6 Plus found speech input at 153 words per minute and a QWERTY keyboard at 52, which is 2.93 times faster. The same study reported 1.30% uncorrected errors for speech and 0.79% for the keyboard.

That study used short English messages on a phone. It did not test Superwhisper or Lazur. Use it as a rough guide, then time yourself with the [speaking vs typing test](/tools/speaking-vs-typing-test).

Accuracy depends on your voice, your microphone and your words. One tl;dv reviewer got about 98% on an everyday paragraph and about 88% on a hard technical script, with no cleanup. That is one person's informal test, not an independent benchmark.

Run your own test. Pick three paragraphs you write often, with the names and terms you use. Dictate each one in both apps and count the fixes. The [dictation accuracy checker](/tools/dictation-accuracy-checker) is a starting point for that.
A common mistake is judging accuracy from one short sentence. Short sentences hide proper-noun errors. Test a full paragraph that includes names.
Who should pick Superwhisper

items: You need dictation with no internet connection on an Apple silicon Mac.
You use Windows, an iPhone or an Android phone and want one license for them.
You want a one-time payment, with Lifetime at $249.99.
You tune models, modes and vocabulary, or transcribe audio files.

blocks.text: Who should pick Lazur

items: You want help with what is on your screen, not only typing.
You learn new Mac apps and want someone to point at the next button.
You want timers, reminders, Calendar events and background research by voice.
You work only on a Mac and do not need a Windows or phone app.

blocks.text: Common mistakes when comparing Lazur and Superwhisper

items: Comparing monthly prices only. Superwhisper's Lifetime plan is a one-time $249.99.
Expecting Lazur to work offline. It sends audio and the screenshot to AI providers while you hold the shortcut.
Expecting Superwhisper to point at buttons. Its plans list modes and context awareness, not step guidance.
Buying Lazur for Windows or iPhone. It is Mac only today.
Using the same key for both apps. Lazur uses fn to dictate and ⌥ ⌘ to ask, so change one shortcut if they overlap.

blocks.text: Can you run Lazur and Superwhisper together?

Yes. One setup that works splits the jobs. Use Superwhisper for long offline dictation and Lazur for questions about the screen. Keep the shortcuts apart. Lazur dictates on hold fn and asks on hold ⌥ ⌘.
Start with one app at a time. Dictate one message with each app. Then ask Lazur about the same message on screen. You will quickly see which app you reach for first.
What to do next

Pick the question you need answered first. If it is whether you can dictate offline, start with Superwhisper's free plan. If it is whether something can help you in the app you are stuck in, start with Lazur's 3-day trial.

[Download Lazur](/download) on your Mac, then try the held shortcut on a real task. Compare the result with the words you have left on Superwhisper's free access. Check [Lazur pricing](/pricing) for plan details before you decide.
If you want other dictation options first, see [Superwhisper alternatives for Mac](/alternatives/superwhisper). It compares prices, platforms and what each app does best.

faq.question: Is Lazur a good Superwhisper alternative?
faq.answer: If you want more than dictation, yes. Lazur dictates in any Mac app with hold fn, and it also answers questions about your screen, points at buttons and guides you one click at a time. If you only need offline transcription across several devices, Superwhisper is the better fit.

faq.question: Does Superwhisper work offline while Lazur does not?
faq.answer: Superwhisper's local models keep audio on your device, and its homepage says it works offline. Lazur sends audio and the screenshot to AI providers while you hold the shortcut, so it needs an internet connection to answer. Nothing is stored, and Lazur says content is never used to train AI models.

faq.question: How much does Superwhisper cost compared with Lazur?
faq.answer: Superwhisper lists Monthly $8.49 per month, Annual $84.99 per year and Lifetime $249.99 one-time, with the same features on each plan. Lazur Pro costs $18/month, or $15/month billed annually. Power costs $120/month, or $96/month billed annually. Check both pricing pages before you buy.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur and Superwhisper together?
faq.answer: Yes, as long as their shortcuts do not clash. Lazur uses hold fn to dictate and hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask. Change one of the shortcuts if the two overlap.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Windows or iPhone?
faq.answer: No. Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available. Superwhisper runs on Mac, Windows 10 and 11, iPhone with iOS 26 or later, and Android phones.

faq.question: Does Superwhisper offer a refund?
faq.answer: Yes. Monthly, Annual and Lifetime plans have a 30-day refund window from the date of first purchase. Renewal charges are not refundable on their own. The plans page does not state a refund policy, so read the manage subscription page too.

faq.question: Is Superwhisper's free plan enough for dictation?
faq.answer: For dictation alone, often yes. The Free plan includes unlimited dictation with local Whisper models, custom vocabulary and up to 2 modes with no AI processing. File transcription and cloud models need Pro.

verdict: Pick Superwhisper if you need dictation without an internet connection, a one-time license, or one license that covers Windows and phones. Pick Lazur if you want a voice assistant on your Mac that sees your screen, answers out loud and points at buttons, with dictation included. If you are unsure, test the same paragraph in both free options first.
